page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m4.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine configured within the KVM hypervisor architecture. Built upon the x86_64 platform, the instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon processors operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs matched with 16.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio that equates to 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware expansion and network capabilities reflect a decoupled design. The instance operates without bundled local disks, requiring network-attached storage volumes for system and data disks. Additionally, the instance incorporates no GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline throughput of 3 Gbps, providing consistent transit for standard distributed cluster traffic and remote storage interactions.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the balanced ratio of dedicated compute to memory avoids the cost overhead associated with memory-bloated or compute-heavy configurations. The lack of bundled local storage ensures operational costs are aligned purely with chosen persistent block volumes. Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m4.xlarge is suited for standard general-purpose workloads, including web application servers, backend microservices, mid-tier relational database environments, container deployment hosts, and CI/CD processing nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m4.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon processors. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 2.7 GHz paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached block storage architectures. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. With its dedicated compute allocation, the instance ensures consistent CPU availability without multi-tenant scheduling contention. From an architectural efficiency perspective, the balanced memory-to-core configuration targets standardized compute workloads without paying for unused RAM or high-frequency silicon tiers. The server fits web serving, containerized enterprise services, intermediate continuous integration and continuous deployment pipelines, application middleware, and small-to-medium relational database workloads.
